chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed al-Hamdani, who reported from Abu Awanah Musa ibn Yusuf ibn Rashid, who reported from Abd al-Salaam ibn Asim, who reported from Ishaq ibn Ismail Hamwayh, who reported from Amru ibn Abu Qais, from Maysarah ibn Habib, from al-Minhal ibn Amru, who said: A man from Banu Tamim reported to me that:

We were with Amirul Mu'mineen Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, at Dhu Qar, and we thought we were to be seized on that day. Then I heard him say: "By Allah! We will overcome this dissenting group. And these two, Talha and Zubair, will be killed and their troops will be uprooted."

Al-Tamimi said: I went to Abdullah ibn al-Abbas and said to him: "Do you hear what your cousin says?" He said: "Do not make haste, wait till we see what happens." When the result of Basrah battle became known, I came to him and said: "Your cousin was right in what he said." He said: "Woe to you! We the companions of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him and his progeny, used to say that he has given him (i.e. Ali) eighty pledges exclusively. Perhaps this was one of them."

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Amirul Mu'mineen: Commander of the Faithful, a title of Imam Ali
key_terms.البصرة: Basrah: site of the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH
key_terms.ثمانين عهدا: eighty pledges: exclusive covenants the Prophet entrusted only to Ali
key_terms.ذي قار: Dhu Qar: location where Ali's army gathered before the Battle of the Camel

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali predict about the Battle of Basrah and what exclusive knowledge did the Prophet give him?
ai.summary: A man from the Banu Tamim tribe recounts being with Imam Ali (AS) at Dhu Qar before the Battle of the Camel. Despite the army's fear, Ali confidently declared by oath that they would overcome the dissenting group and that Talha and Zubair would be killed and their army uprooted. After the prediction came true at Basrah, Abdullah ibn al-Abbas explained that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWAS) had exclusively entrusted Ali with eighty pledges, and this foreknowledge was likely one of them. The hadith highlights Ali's divinely-granted knowledge of future events and his unique station among the Prophet's companions.
word_analysis: and these two will be killed
